summary: Tested newly added DNS/MX-record domain validation on POST /api/auth/signup. Created backend/tests/test_signup_domain_validation.py (11 tests) covering fake-domain rejection (en/de/es localization), no-user-created verification via direct MongoDB query + login-fails check, valid-domain (gmail.com/outlook.com) signup success within time budget, duplicate-email regression, and non-interference with google_auth, apple_auth, and forgot-password. All 11 tests passed. Outbound DNS resolution works fine in this sandbox (verified NXDOMAIN and MX lookups directly), so fail-open concerns didn't materialize.
critical_code_review_comments: _has_valid_mail_domain correctly fails open on any exception other than NXDOMAIN (including DNS timeouts), matching the requirement.
The check is placed as the very first line in signup(), before duplicate-email check, exactly as specified.
google_auth, apple_auth, forgot-password, verify-email, resend-verification were all confirmed unmodified/unaffected by this change.
No hardcoded values; dns.resolver lifetime=3.0s timeout is reasonable to avoid blocking signup.
seed_data_creation: Test users created with TEST_ prefix on gmail.com/outlook.com domains during test run (transient, not cleaned up but harmless test data in DB).
context_for_next_testing_agent: DNS validation feature for signup is fully working and verified. No issues found. Sandbox has working outbound DNS access, so both MX-lookup success and NXDOMAIN paths were genuinely exercised (not just fail-open fallback).
